accepted_state: Initial eight-area capability expansion is complete.
Default operating phase is hardening, consolidation, outcome validation, and gap-oriented learning rather than default skill expansion.
GitHub mutation guard contracts remain CI-validated; native provider interception is deferred unless a controllable dispatcher surface becomes available.
Every live skill entrypoint has a consolidation classification and routing overlap clusters have machine-readable primary ownership rules.
Skill Acquisition is phase-gated and must not trigger a new expansion wave without explicit request or demonstrated gap.
Agent Engineering treats executor/model claims as candidate state and requires evidence-appropriate promotion into durable accepted state.
Tracing/evaluation, context engineering, controlled self-improvement, and task-scoped tool-authority contracts remain CI-validated.
Security Engineering distinguishes technical capability possession from current-task action authority.
Multi-agent delegation now attenuates authority: a child capability envelope must be a subset of the parent's currently authorized envelope.
Workflow handoff may transfer control but does not automatically transfer or expand tool authority.
Child re-delegation requires explicit permission and remains recursively bounded by the original authority chain.
Delegated workers must escalate blocked authority needs rather than self-authorize, and should return compact provenance, evidence, uncertainty, and blocked actions.
Delegated claims remain candidate state until verified at the evidence level appropriate to the claim.
Executable continuity checkpoint state remains CI-validated.
unresolved_risks: The public Core cannot intercept every native provider/tool/sub-agent call unless the host routes execution through an enforceable dispatcher or service ACL seam.
Eight skills remain NEEDS_EVIDENCE and should not be promoted to stronger consolidation decisions without representative outcomes.

Routing, verified-state, trajectory, context, self-improvement, tool-authority, and delegation-authority contracts remain contract-level refinements until representative real-task evidence accumulates.
Some host multi-agent surfaces may not expose child capability envelopes or re-delegation metadata, so universal enforcement cannot be claimed.
Delegation can add coordination cost and authority complexity; smallest-sufficient topology remains the default.

next_executable_step.action: When ordinary work genuinely benefits from a sub-agent or handoff, delegate the smallest subtask with an attenuated authority envelope, require compact provenance/evidence on return, and escalate any missing authority instead of silently expanding it. Record genuine coordination wins, blocked privilege escalations, authority friction, rework, or regressions as outcome evidence; do not create multi-agent work merely to manufacture evidence.
